headline: 12kg LPG cylinder price rises by Tk 252 to Tk 1,837
summary: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission has increased retail prices for October, citing higher Saudi Contract Prices and freight costs.
details: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has raised the retail price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for October. The most widely used 12kg cylinder has seen a price hike of Tk 252, bringing its cost to Tk 1,837.
The new prices take effect from 6pm on Sunday. Private LPG retail prices, including VAT, have been set at Tk 153.06 per kg for October, an increase of Tk 20.94 from September's rate of Tk 132.12.
Other cylinder sizes have also seen adjustments: a 5.5kg cylinder now costs Tk 842, while 12.5kg, 15kg, and 16kg cylinders are priced at Tk 1,913, Tk 2,296, and Tk 2,449 respectively.
The price of autogas used in vehicles has also increased significantly, rising by Tk 11.53 per litre to reach Tk 84.62.
BERC stated the adjustment was based on the Saudi Contract Price (Saudi CP) for propane and butane. The average Saudi CP increased by $64.75 per tonne in one month.
Additionally, BERC considered a higher freight and importers' premium of $250 per tonne for October, compared to $160 in September.
The price of government-supplied LPG remains unchanged, with a 12.5kg government cylinder staying at Tk 776.93.
BERC has warned that bottled LPG, reticulated LPG, and autogas cannot be sold at prices higher than those set by the commission.

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has raised the retail price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for October. The most widely used 12kg cylinder has seen a price hike of Tk 252, bringing its cost to Tk 1,837.

The new prices take effect from 6pm on Sunday. Private LPG retail prices, including VAT, have been set at Tk 153.06 per kg for October, an increase of Tk 20.94 from September's rate of Tk 132.12.

Other cylinder sizes have also seen adjustments: a 5.5kg cylinder now costs Tk 842, while 12.5kg, 15kg, and 16kg cylinders are priced at Tk 1,913, Tk 2,296, and Tk 2,449 respectively.

The price of autogas used in vehicles has also increased significantly, rising by Tk 11.53 per litre to reach Tk 84.62.

BERC stated the adjustment was based on the Saudi Contract Price (Saudi CP) for propane and butane. The average Saudi CP increased by $64.75 per tonne in one month.

Additionally, BERC considered a higher freight and importers' premium of $250 per tonne for October, compared to $160 in September.

The price of government-supplied LPG remains unchanged, with a 12.5kg government cylinder staying at Tk 776.93.

BERC has warned that bottled LPG, reticulated LPG, and autogas cannot be sold at prices higher than those set by the commission.

headline_marked: Ex-MP Akhtaruzzaman [[denied bail and sent to jail]] over airport incident
headline: Ex-MP Akhtaruzzaman denied bail and sent to jail over airport incident
summary: Jamaat-e-Islami alleges the arrest of the retired army major and lawmaker was a result of 'policymaking-level directives' and political vengeance.
details: Former lawmaker and retired army major Akhtaruzzaman has been sent to jail after his bail application was denied by the court.
The arrest follows an incident at the airport where Akhtaruzzaman and other lawmakers had to wait for hours for their luggage due to mismanagement and a shortage of trolleys.

Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar alleged at a press conference that the arrest was an act of political vengeance and was driven by 'directives' from the government's policymaking level.
Porwar claimed that the airport's civil aviation minister had falsely accused Akhtaruzzaman of physically assaulting someone at the airport, calling the claim '1,000 percent false'.
Jamaat leaders criticized the authorities for transporting Akhtaruzzaman to court in handcuffs, a helmet, and a bulletproof jacket, questioning if he was a 'hardened criminal'.
The party demanded his immediate release on bail and that he be granted division facilities in jail.
During the press conference, Porwar also expressed 'disgust' over the recent hike in LPG cylinder prices, calling it an additional burden on the public.
He alleged that syndicates and political interests were behind the price hikes, turning Bangladesh into a 'political marketplace'.
